MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Bus Stop Ridership Estimates: Beginning 2024
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset includes estimated boardings for bus stop level ridership. Each record represents ridership activity for a route, direction, and stop during a specific month-day of week-hour. Boarding estimates are derived from Automatic Passenger Counters (APCs) that are in use on the buses along MTA’s routes.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Customer Feedback: Beginning 2018
MTA Bus Stops.description: The Customer Feedback dataset provides a summary of customer feedback recorded in the MTA’s Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system. Customers may submit feedback about MTA services by phone, through online form, by mail, or through other customer service channels. Each submission is entered as a case in the CRM system and assigned attributes such as agency, date received, and category.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Bus Schedules: 2026
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset includes data for all bus schedules. It includes rows for each scheduled timepoint stop on a trip.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA NaviLens Usage
MTA Bus Stops.description: Navilens usage data contains records of scan events (each row represents a time a NaviLens code was scanned). Scan records include the code identifier, the type of asset scanned (e.g., bus stop, bus vehicle, subway station, train car, or vehicle feature), the app used (NaviLens vs. NaviLens GO), the device language setting at time of scan, and timestamps. For certain asset types, scan events are also enriched with location fields such as bus stop identifiers and names or subway station identifiers and names. This data supports evaluation of the NaviLens deployment and related project reporting

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA NaviLens Feedback Survey
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset contains responses from the MTA NaviLens feedback survey, which collects customer feedback on NaviLens and NaviLens GO, two accessibility and wayfinding smartphone apps used with brightly colored NaviLens codes installed across select MTA subway stations, subway cars, bus stops, and buses. This data supports evaluation of the NaviLens deployment and related project reporting, including work funded through the USDOT SMART Grant.

MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset contains point features for bus stops used on each route and direction within a bundle, including stop usage flags (revenue, timepoint, boarding, alighting, is in CBD) and basic route descriptors for mapping and stop-level analyses.

MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset contains records of violations, including issued violations and those rejected for business reasons. Each row represents an individual violation of a vehicle double parked or blocking a bus lane or bus stop.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Central Business District Bus Speeds: Beginning 2023
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset provides aggregated data on how fast MTA buses are traveling between major stops (timepoints) on a bus route for every route operated by NYCT and MTABC. These segments are categorized as either CBD or Non-CBD. The dataset provides the average speed in miles per hour and the number of bus trips for each bus route, aggregated by month, day type, hour of day, and relation to the CBD.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Bus Automated Camera Enforced Routes: Beginning October 2019
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset provides information on the implementation dates of Automated Bus Lane Enforcement (ABLE) and Automated Camera Enforcement (ACE) systems across MTA bus routes. ABLE, launched as a pilot in 2019, and later expanded and rebranded as ACE in 2024, uses cameras mounted on buses to capture vehicles obstructing bus lanes, double parked, or parked illegally at bus stops.

MTA Bus Stops.name: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership: Beginning 2025
MTA Bus Stops.description: This dataset provides subway ridership estimates on an hourly basis by subway station complex and class of fare payment.

MTA Subway Stations.description: This dataset represents each of the General Orders (GOs) that were created for the subway system since 2019 and their respective impacts on the system. GOs are made to notify operating personnel about how, when, and where service is being changed for work being done in the subway system.

MTA Subway Stations.name: MTA Subway Station Amenities: Beginning May 2026
MTA Subway Stations.description: The MTA Subway Station Amenities data provides information about amenities available at subway stations across the New York City transit system.

MTA Subway Stations.name: MTA DOS Track Linear Referencing System (LRS)
MTA Subway Stations.description: This dataset includes track geometries for the MTA NYCT Subway system, including both mainline and yard tracks. It also includes stationing measurement data (in feet) for the tracks.

MTA Subway Stations.name: MTA Subway Origin-Destination Ridership Estimate: Beginning 2026
MTA Subway Stations.description: This dataset provides an estimate of subway travel patterns based on scaled-up OMNY and MetroCard return swipe data. It provides estimated passenger volumes for all populated origin-destination (O-D) pairs aggregated by month, day of the week, and hour of day. It also provides the name, ID, and approximate latitude and longitude of the origin and destination subway complexes.

MTA Subway Stations.name: MTA Pulse Survey: Beginning 2025
MTA Subway Stations.description: The Pulse Survey dataset provides customer sentiment and satisfaction results across MTA service modes. The dataset is organized as survey output records (not individual-level responses) and includes fields such as month, time period, mode, bus type, question text, category, measure, score grain, score type, score, and sample size.

This dataset contains encompasses the ACEP investment budgets across our Capital Plans.

The data describes the planned projects and provide information about the status of Project Budgets, Scopes and Schedules. This view provides data for the current quarter only.

MTA GTFS.name: MTA Subway Paths: Beginning 2019
MTA GTFS.description:
This dataset is a table of each distinct set of stations, or path, made by all normal and extra subway trips that run in service, excepting those that skipped one or more planned stops due to service disruptions.

There is a row for each subway stop made by a stop path. These rows also contain the unique id for each path, the number of stops made by the path, the distance in miles along the path, the origin and destination stations, and the order a stop is in the stop path.
